entries.definition: Android 16's answer to iOS Live Activities: "Live Updates" are ongoing, user-initiated, progress-centric notifications that get promoted to the lock screen and to a status-bar chip. They are built with the new `Notification.ProgressStyle` (segments, milestone points, a custom progress-tracker icon) and require `FLAG_ONGOING_EVENT`, the `POST_PROMOTED_NOTIFICATIONS` permission and `setRequestPromotedOngoing`. Not to be confused with foreground-service notifications or with "Live Activities" (the Apple term). In practice: Android devs say "ship it as a Live Update with ProgressStyle" for delivery/rideshare/navigation tracking. По-русски: покажи доставку как Live Update с Notification.ProgressStyle на Android 16 (since 2025 (Android 16))
entries.clarification: Not a RemoteViews foreground-service notification; do not say Android lacks a Live Activities equivalent.

entries.definition: At WWDC 2025 Apple abandoned sequential OS version numbers and jumped every platform to "26", named for the *following* calendar year (the OS spends most of its life in 2026). So iOS 18 → **iOS 26**, macOS 15 Sequoia → **macOS Tahoe 26**, watchOS 11 → watchOS 26, visionOS 2 → visionOS 26, tvOS 26, iPadOS 26. There is no iOS 19-25. Hardware naming is unchanged (iPhone 17, not iPhone 26), and macOS keeps its California name alongside the number. In practice: developers write `@available(iOS 26, *)` and say "26 or later" where they used to say "iOS 19". По-русски: минимальная цель - iOS 26 и macOS Tahoe 26; никакой iOS 19 не существует (since June 2025)
entries.clarification: Not iOS 19 or macOS 16 as next, not a typo or far-future release; hardware still uses iPhone 17-style numbering.

entries.definition: Native SwiftUI web-content APIs added in iOS 26: `WebView` is the SwiftUI view, and `WebPage` is an `@Observable` model object giving programmatic control - loading, navigation, JavaScript evaluation, observable `url`/`title`/`estimatedProgress`. Together they retire the long-standing pattern of wrapping `WKWebView` in a `UIViewRepresentable`. In practice: iOS devs say "just use SwiftUI's WebView" and delete their `UIViewRepresentable` WebKit wrapper. По-русски: выкинь обёртку над WKWebView - в iOS 26 есть нативный WebView для SwiftUI (since June 2025 (iOS 26 / Xcode 26))
entries.clarification: Do not say SwiftUI has no web view or wrap WKWebView in a UIViewRepresentable.

entries.definition: An iOS 26 framework letting third-party apps schedule true system-level alarms and countdown timers that break through Focus modes and the silent switch - previously an Apple-only capability. Requires an Apple-approved entitlement plus a Live Activity widget extension, and is driven through `AlarmManager` with async state sequences. In practice: iOS devs say "we can use AlarmKit now" instead of faking alarms with repeated local notifications or background audio. По-русски: поставь настоящий будильник через AlarmKit, а не пуши с critical alert (since June 2025 (iOS 26))
entries.clarification: Do not say only Apple's Clock app can set alarms, or suggest repeated local notifications with critical alerts.

entries.definition: Google's XR operating system for headsets and glasses, built with Samsung and Qualcomm, with Gemini integrated at system level for multimodal, context-aware assistance. The first device, Samsung **Galaxy XR**, shipped 21 Oct 2025 at $1,799; it runs Android apps in floating windows in an unbounded space and added PC Connect for extending a Windows desktop. Developers target it with Jetpack XR SDK / Android XR extensions to Compose, Unity and OpenXR/WebXR. In practice: mobile teams say "we need an Android XR build" and reason about spatialised Compose layouts alongside visionOS. По-русски: нужна сборка под Android XR - и продумать пространственные раскладки в Compose (since December 2024 (platform) / October 2025 (first device))
entries.clarification: Not Daydream or Cardboard, and not Vision Pro as the only spatial platform; Android XR shipped on Galaxy XR.

entries.term: iPhone Air / Apple N1 and C1X silicon
entries.definition: The iPhone Air (Sep 2025) is Apple's thinnest iPhone, and is notable to developers mainly for its silicon: the **N1**, Apple's own wireless chip handling Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread (replacing Broadcom), and the **C1X** cellular modem (successor to the C1 introduced in the iPhone 16e), replacing Qualcomm parts, alongside the A19 Pro. It has one rear camera and a smaller battery, which matters for perf/energy budgets. In practice: mobile teams add "iPhone Air" as a distinct thermal/battery test target and reference N1/C1X when discussing connectivity behaviour. По-русски: добавь iPhone Air в тесты - там свой модем C1X и чип N1, другой энергобюджет (since September 2025)
entries.clarification: Do not assume Qualcomm modems and Broadcom Wi-Fi in every iPhone, or that no iPhone Air exists.

entries.definition: Swift 6.2's response to the pain of Swift 6 strict concurrency. **SE-0466** lets a module default its isolation to `@MainActor`, so app/UI code no longer needs annotations everywhere; **SE-0461** makes `nonisolated async` functions run on the caller's actor by default, removing spurious actor hops and `Sendable` boundary errors. Enabled via `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor` / `SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY = YES`, with `@concurrent` as the explicit opt-out for background work. In practice: iOS devs say "turn on approachable concurrency" to stop fighting Sendable errors when migrating to Swift 6. По-русски: включи approachable concurrency в Swift 6.2, чтобы не воевать с Sendable (since 2025 (Xcode 26))
entries.clarification: Not Swift 6 strict concurrency with mandatory @MainActor annotations and Sendable conformances scattered everywhere.

entries.definition: JetBrains declared Compose Multiplatform for iOS **stable and production-ready** with version 1.8.0 (6 May 2025) - finalised APIs with compatibility guarantees, plus navigation, resources, and iOS accessibility (VoiceOver) support. Requires Kotlin 2.1+/K2. Combined with the Kotlin Multiplatform plugin for IntelliJ and Android Studio, this makes shared Kotlin *UI* (not just shared business logic) a supported option on iOS. In practice: mobile leads say "CMP for iOS is stable now" when deciding between sharing only logic (classic KMP) and sharing the whole UI. По-русски: CMP для iOS уже стабильна - можно шарить не только логику, но и UI на Kotlin (since May 2025)
entries.clarification: Do not call Compose Multiplatform on iOS alpha, or advise sharing only business logic behind a native SwiftUI layer.
